Theme 084 · Art movements & eras

Swiss Grid

International Typographic Style played straight: a visible 12-module grid, flush-left grotesk, giant numerals and a single spot colour. Every beat snaps to a module, so the one row that turns coral in an otherwise objective table is the whole story.

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

Words stack on quarter notes, "minute." switches to italic serif on the last beat; the coral CTA block snaps from width 0 to 5 modules on the final downbeat.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Visible grid — 12 × 12 modules of 80 px, hairlines at 7–16 % opacity
  • Giant numeral — one number per beat, 300–600 px Manrope 800, tight tracking
  • Flush-left headline — ragged right, never centred, one serif italic word
  • Timetable table — objective rows of metrics in mono; the anomaly row floods coral
  • Caption column — mono figure notes parked in the rightmost 3 modules
  • Module button — rectangular CTA exactly 5 modules wide, arrow in mono

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Grid stroke-on — hairlines draw 0→100 % in 0.5 s, power2.out, staggered 0.03 s — finishes on beat 1
  • Module snap — blocks move only in whole-module steps (80 px), steps(4) or expo.out 0.25 s, one step per 8th note
  • Row flood — coral background scaleX 0→1 from the left, 0.5 s power3.inOut = one beat at 120 BPM

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Swiss objectivity reads as honesty: nothing decorates the data, so a monitoring product looks precise and trustworthy. Risk: it can feel cold or generic-corporate; the oversized numerals and the one-colour discipline are what keep it a poster rather than a slide.

Adapt to your product: Replace the table rows with your own KPIs or features and keep exactly one spot colour for the moment your product intervenes. Any screenshot you add should be cropped to whole grid modules.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Typographic_Style — grid, flush-left sans, asymmetric layout, objectivity · https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josef_M%C3%BCller-Brockmann — Der Film poster and Grid Systems in Graphic Design
